text:
The Golden Knights' power play opened the door on Wednesday and Ivan Barbashev walked through it twice. Vegas beat Utah 5-3 at T-Mobile Arena for a fourth straight win, and the scoreline was closer than the game.

It started 2:15 in. Mitch Marner drove into the slot, sold the shot and found Jack Eichel, who one-timed it top shelf, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger described it from the press box. Lawson Crouse tied it at 8:07 on a backhand, and for a period Utah looked comfortable. The second period was where Vegas took the game, out-chancing the Mammoth 1.57 to 0.65 in expected goals (the quality of chances). Victor Olofsson scored on another power play at 3:07, then set up both of Barbashev's goals, at 4:51 and 8:16, for a 4-1 lead.

Utah's depth kept pushing back. Jack McBain scored late in the second and assisted on Dmitri Simashev's goal at 9:07 of the third, a 6% chance that made it 4-3. The building did not have long to worry: Brett Howden tipped in a Marner feed 72 seconds later. Marner finished with three assists, Olofsson with a goal and two, and Olofsson's line was on the ice for 3.46 expected goals for and 0.31 against.

Even strength was close, 1.93 expected goals to 1.87. The difference was special teams and finishing in front of the net: Vegas went 2 for 4 on the power play while Utah drew one chance all night, and Vegas totalled 4.69 expected goals to 2.25 overall. Our deserved-to-win measure (the share of replays of every shot a team wins) had Vegas at 68%. Sebastian Cossa allowed 1.7 goals more than his 28 shots deserved, and his best stop, on a 39% Mark Stone look in the second, was the only reason the margin wasn't wider. Carter Hart saw just 17 shots and allowed three.

Four straight for Vegas, with the power play humming and Marner settling into the role the Knights paid for. Utah leaves with a respectable night from its third line and questions about how few chances its top players created.
headline: Barbashev twice as Vegas makes it four straight
